body:
# Baꜥal: the stories first, then the spelling

You cannot weigh an accent without knowing what it carries. Here is what **Baꜥal** has been carrying.

## The Stories That Carry the Name

**Against Prince Yamm.** Before Baꜥal could rule, the Sea had to be beaten.  In the opening tablets of the cycle (KTU 1. 1–1.

**The Cedar House on Zaphon.** Victory leaves Baꜥal homeless: a king without a palace is a king without a throne.  He sends ꜥAnat to plead before Ēl, but it is Asherah — the diplomatic wife of the old god — who finally secures the decree (KTU 1. 4 iv–v).

**Death in the Mouth of Mot.** When the palace is finished, Death itself sends an invitation.  Mōt — whose throat is a lion's and whose gullet is a whale's — demands that Baꜥal come down into the realm of dust and drought (KTU 1. 5 i).

## And Here Is What the Spelling Preserves

Against those stories, the attestation: **Βαάλ**, in the attestation KTU (Ugaritic texts) and CIS give us. The name means "Canaanite storm and fertility god; the title "Lord" (baʿlu) was also applied to local deities".


## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Baꜥal
- **ASCII form:** baal
- **Meaning:** "Canaanite storm and fertility god; the title "Lord" (baʿlu) was also applied to local deities"
- **Domain of influence:** Storm God, Lord of the Heavens
- **Pantheon:** Canaanite
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** 𐎁𐎓𐎍
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 72 of 546

## The Name Travels

Baꜥal is inseparable from the older West Semitic storm god Hadad/Haddu; in texts and inscriptions the two names are often combined as Baꜥal-Haddu.  In Mesopotamia he was equated with Adad (dIM), and in Egypt he influenced the Levantine storm god imported during the New Kingdom.

## The Address It Earned

The temple of **Baꜥal** stands at [/baal/](/baal/) — [lore](/baal/lore/), [scholars](/baal/scholars/), [patterns](/baal/patterns/) — because a name carrying this much story deserves more than a parking page. What survives here cannot be shown in ASCII: a feature of the original that the fallback alphabet flattens. That is the Tier-1 test, and this name passes it without argument.

## The Sources Are Open

The myths above are retold from the temple's record; the primary voices are in the [Sacred Texts](/texts/): [Enūma Eliš](/texts/enuma-elish/). Nothing in this file outranks them.
